questions.title: What do you do with your second ball if your first ball went out?
questions.question: You hit a second ball because you thought your first one might be out of bounds. Now you see your first ball is definitely out. What happens next?

choices.text: You keep playing the second ball and add one shot to your score.
You pick up the second ball and drop a new ball where your first ball went out.
You can use your first ball and don’t get a penalty.

questions.explanation: If your first ball went out of bounds, your second ball (the provisional ball) becomes the one you play, and you get one extra shot as a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When your ball is outside the edges of the golf course, like over a fence or white line.
A second ball you play if you think your first ball might be lost or out of bounds.

questions.teachingTip: Practise hitting a provisional ball so children know what to do if their first ball goes over a boundary.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they can keep using the original ball if they find it, even if it’s out of bounds.
Some might believe they need to drop a new ball instead of using the provisional ball.

questions.title: What happens to your provisional ball?
questions.question: After you've played a provisional ball because your first shot might be out of bounds, what do you do if it's clear your first ball is definitely out?

choices.text: Your provisional ball becomes your ball in play and you get a one-stroke penalty.
You must pick up your provisional ball and drop another ball at the out of bounds spot.
You can keep playing your original ball with no penalty.

questions.explanation: If your original ball is confirmed out of bounds, your provisional ball becomes your ball in play, and you must add a one-stroke penalty.
